introduction: On this Sunday, Elijah prays over the dead son of a widow, and God gives the boy back to his mother. In the Gospel, Jesus meets a funeral procession at the town of Nain; moved with compassion for the widowed mother, he says, Young man, arise, and gives him back to her. Paul tells how God called him, once a persecutor, by grace. Let us praise God, who has visited his people.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, God has visited his people. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church: that she may share the compassion of Christ for all who mourn. Let us pray to the Lord.
For widows, widowers and parents who have lost a child: that the Lord may comfort them. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who are dying and those who care for them: that they may trust in the Lord of life. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who have turned away from God, as Paul once did: that his grace may call them back. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may believe that Jesus raises us up, and that joy comes in the morning. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord God, your Son had compassion on the widow of Nain and raised her son to life. Comfort all who mourn, and raise us up on the last day. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Do not weep
reflection.body:
In the first reading, a widow who had taken in the prophet Elijah loses her only son. In her grief, she turns on Elijah. Elijah takes the boy, lays him on his own bed, and cries out to God: "LORD my God, please let this child's soul come into him again." God hears him, and the boy revives. Elijah gives him back to his mother, saying, "Behold, your son lives."

In the Gospel, Jesus arrives at the gate of the town of Nain just as a funeral procession is coming out. The dead man is "the only born son of his mother, and she was a widow." In that society, a widow who lost her only son lost not only the person she loved, but also her protection and her future.

No one asks Jesus for anything. He sees her, and Luke tells us: "When the Lord saw her, he had compassion on her and said to her", "Don't cry." Then he touches the bier, and says, "Young man, I tell you, arise!" The dead man sits up and begins to speak, "Then he gave him to his mother."

The crowd sees in this the action of God himself: "A great prophet has arisen among us!" and "God has visited his people!" Jesus is greater than Elijah: he does not need to pray at length; he speaks with his own authority over death.

This Gospel is a source of comfort for all who mourn. Jesus sees our grief and is moved by it. And it is a sign of the resurrection he promises to all who believe in him.

The psalm sings of this hope: "Weeping may stay for the night, but joy comes in the morning." Paul tells how God reached out to him when he was a persecutor of the Church: God "called me through his grace."

This week, pray for someone who is grieving, and if you can, visit them. And bring your own losses to Jesus, who has compassion on you.
